title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-16
ranking_explanation: All entries were taken from the current GitHub Trending daily page at capture time, then ordered by the page-reported daily star gains in descending order. Gains are partial-day figures, not a full-day close. Current star totals, languages, and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated with GitHub REST API.
global_caveat: Snapshot is partial-day. The GitHub Search API recent-created query returned a noisy, clone-heavy set, so no additional candidates were included. Repository purpose for narration is based on current GitHub Trending descriptions and README review for the five largest daily gainers; no DeepWiki enrichment was used.

themes.title: Agent integration and interaction
themes.content: Projects connect agents to office capabilities, user interfaces, browsers, developer tools, or media workflows.

themes.title: Agent quality, evaluation, and review
themes.content: SkillEvaluator measures skill quality and impact; Open Code Review adds deterministic review structure; Plannotator supplies human feedback.

themes.title: Reusable skills for specialized tasks
themes.content: The list applies skills and multi-agent workflows to trading, design, video editing, research writing, and cross-source topic research.

themes.title: Established and domain-specific projects beyond agent tooling
themes.content: The historical atlas, Svelte framework, and Docker management interface are non-agent or conventional developer projects in the same daily list.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily snapshot captured 2026-11-16 17:33 UTC; date range 2026-11-16 through 2026-11-16. Ranked by daily GitHub Trending star gains.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Univer led the captured daily list with +1,878 stars, ahead of NVIDIA SkillEvaluator (+953) and Alibaba Open Code Review (+946). The clearest common thread is tooling that makes coding agents more usable and accountable—through application integrations, review/evaluation workflows, and reusable task skills—alongside a smaller set of established or domain-specific projects.

sections.title: Top Repositories
sections.content: Fourteen repositories, ordered by descending daily stars gained; per-repository sections follow.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.
sections.content: An Office SDK for embedding editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into products and agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: The day's largest gain; its README positions the open-source SDK as a way to connect office capabilities to applications and agents.

sections.title: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
sections.description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior.
sections.content: A three-tier framework for validating skills, finding semantic overlap, and testing their effects on agent task results.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest gain; the README describes a pipeline from checks and deduplication to live evaluation of skill impact.
sections.unique_caveat: Live Tier 3 evaluation requires a provider, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default), according to the README.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
sections.content: A code-review tool pairing deterministic checks with a tool-using LLM agent and line-level comments.
sections.why_notable: Nearly tied for second in daily gains; its hybrid architecture targets more structured, repeatable reviews than a free-form agent pass.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders — market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, screeners, and trading strategy development.
sections.content: Claude Code workflows for market review, risk management, trade planning, and journaling.
sections.why_notable: A strong domain-specific skills project; its README frames the toolkit as decision-process support, not a buy/sell signal service.
sections.unique_caveat: The project says it is not a signal service or a promise of profitability; its workflows support human decision-making.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.content: An MCP server and CLI that let coding agents inspect and control a live Chrome browser using DevTools.
sections.why_notable: Combines a major daily gain with a concrete bridge from agent workflows to browser debugging, performance, and network inspection.
sections.unique_caveat: The README warns that MCP clients can inspect browser-instance contents; usage statistics are collected by default, with an opt-out.

sections.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
sections.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
sections.content: An event-based protocol for connecting AI agents with user-facing applications.
sections.why_notable: A high-momentum infrastructure project focused on the agent-to-UI interaction layer.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.
sections.content: A workspace for annotating agent plans and code changes and returning feedback to the agent.
sections.why_notable: Represents the human-review side of agent workflows: people can shape plans and review diffs before feeding decisions back.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
sections.content: Agent Skills for working with Google's Stitch MCP server, packaged for multiple coding-agent clients.
sections.why_notable: Shows the Agent Skills format being used as a portable distribution layer across different coding agents.

sections.title: kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill
sections.description: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.
sections.content: A local video-editing toolkit exposing 42 FFmpeg operations through agent tools and an MCP server.
sections.why_notable: A focused example of agent skills wrapping mature command-line tooling; the project describes a local, no-cloud, no-API-key workflow.

sections.title: google-research/paper-orchestra
sections.description: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
sections.content: A multi-agent framework for automated research-paper writing.
sections.why_notable: Extends the multi-agent pattern into a specialized research-writing workflow.

sections.title: DeanChensj/jiangshan-map
sections.description: 江山时序 · 中国历史交互地图时间轴 (403 BCE – Present) | Interactive Historical Atlas of China across 18 dynasties, 198 territory snapshots, ancient-to-modern place genealogy & classical poetry routes
sections.content: An interactive historical atlas of China, spanning dynastic territory snapshots and historical place-name links.
sections.why_notable: A data-rich mapping project that stands apart from the agent-tool cluster while still drawing meaningful daily interest.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
sections.content: A research skill that gathers signals from Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket, and the web.
sections.why_notable: Applies agent skills to cross-source topic research and grounded synthesis.

sections.title: sveltejs/svelte
sections.description: web development for the rest of us
sections.content: The Svelte frontend framework.
sections.why_notable: An established framework provides a non-agent counterpoint in a list otherwise dominated by agent-adjacent tooling.

sections.title: getarcaneapp/arcane
sections.description: Modern Docker Management, Designed for Everyone
sections.content: A user-friendly interface for managing Docker.
sections.why_notable: A conventional self-hosting/developer-operations tool at the lower end of this day's star-gain ranking.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: The dominant cluster is agent-facing software: office and UI interfaces, reusable skills, review/approval loops, and browser/code tooling. TypeScript and Python each appear in 5 of 14 repositories; Go and JavaScript each appear in 2. This is a count of the listed repositories, not a measure of all GitHub activity.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's list is less about a single new model than the infrastructure around agents: connecting them to real interfaces, giving people review points, and testing whether reusable skills improve outcomes. Office, browser, code-review, trading, and media workflows show how quickly that infrastructure is being packaged into specific developer products; the atlas, Svelte, and Docker entries show that conventional projects still share the day's attention.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-11-16 at 17:33 UTC. GitHub REST repository metadata and default-branch commit endpoints were checked for all 14 repositories. GitHub Search API query created:2026-11-14..2026-11-16 stars:>=50 pushed:>=2026-11-14 was checked for recently created projects; its results were noisy and clone-heavy, so no extra entries were added. Daily gains come from the matching GitHub Trending view; totals, languages, and commit SHAs were corroborated against REST API at capture time. No prior-window comparison is claimed.
